item.title: Jurors deliberate in the trial of rap icon Tupac Shakur's killing
item.description: Attorneys on Monday gave their closing arguments in the trial of Tupac Shakur's killing. The rap star was gunned down in a gang-related drive-by shooting in Las Vegas in 1996.
item.content:encoded: Attorneys on Monday gave their closing arguments in the trial of Tupac Shakur's killing. The rap star was gunned down in a gang-related drive-by shooting in Las Vegas in 1996.

item.title: Paperwork, lines, hours on hold: There's a 'Time Tax' on Americans who need help most
item.description: Annie Lowrey explores the administrative burdens people face applying for government benefits. It's not just about wasted time: "When the government treats us like this, we don't trust it," she says.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: At least 15 people missing after Grand Canyon flash flood
item.description: Several people are missing or unaccounted for after severe flash flooding in the Grand Canyon on Saturday caused significant damage.

item.title: The U.S.-Venezuela oil deal won't lower your gas prices. Here's what you need to know
item.description: The Trump administration announced a deal Friday to develop a vast amount of Venezuela's oil reserves, with the U.S. taking a majority stake. Energy experts say there are many reasons to be skeptical.

item.description: After internal pushback amongst top military officials over gutting a civilian protection program, the Pentagon is looking at partially restoring it.

item.title: Arizona's taps won't run dry, but water bills will go up under federal plan for Colorado River
item.description: New federal rules mean Arizona will be getting a lot less water from the Colorado river. City leaders say they've been planning for years and no one will run out, but keeping taps flowing is expensive.
